info.title: EQ Scoring Platform — Human-Likeness & AI Text Benchmark API
info.description: Human-likeness scoring and AI text benchmark API. Score AI-generated text against real human personality profiles (EQ, formality, directness, hesitation, response-timing cadence) to measure how human your AI writing sounds before you ship it. Built for autonomous agents and AI text humanizer pipelines: free stateless scoring at /api/score, paid validated benchmarks via machine-to-machine On-chain settlement with x402 support — the default path is gasless USDC on Base (unpaid calls to /api/simulate return HTTP 402 with machine-readable payment requirements; sign the Base requirement and retry once with PAYMENT-SIGNATURE). Legacy SOL and X-PAYMENT clients remain compatible. Interactive API docs are available at /api/docs. Permanent tool setup (wire it in once and explicitly authorize a dedicated USDC-on-Base burner wallet so the SDK can sign paid calls without a human): see the 'Permanent tool setup' section of /llms.txt and the crawlable guide at /guides/permanent-agent-tool-setup.html. Live network stats (real ledger aggregates) at /api/stats; runnable Python/JS quickstart examples ship in the repo under examples/.

post.description:
Buy a prepaid bundle of basic-score credits at a discount.

One x402 payment (SOL or USDC) buys the published number of credits,
credited to the paying wallet. The response contains a SECRET
`bundle_token` — store it; it is shown exactly once. Redeem credits by
sending the `X-BUNDLE-TOKEN` header on POST /api/simulate (basic tier).
Check remaining credits at GET /api/bundle/balance.

## Default x402 v2 payment flow

1. **Quote** — POST /api/bundle with no payment header. Read the full
   HTTP **402** body and select the first `accepts` entry: Base USDC
   (`network: eip155:8453`).
2. **Sign** — sign that entry's exact EIP-3009
   `TransferWithAuthorization` fields. The wallet needs Base USDC but
   no ETH; the facilitator submits the authorization.
3. **Build** — create the canonical x402 v2 payload using the full
   response's `resource`, the selected entry as `accepted`, the signed
   `payload`, and `extensions` when present:

```json
{"x402Version":2,
 "resource":{"url":"https://eqbuilder.dev/api/bundle"},
 "accepted":{"scheme":"exact","network":"eip155:8453","amount":"<live amount>","payTo":"<live address>","asset":"<Base USDC contract>"},
 "payload":{"signature":"0x...65-byte EIP-712 signature...","authorization":{"from":"0xYourAddress","to":"0xPayToAddress","value":"<live amount>","validAfter":"0","validBefore":"<future unix>","nonce":"0x...32 random bytes..."}},
 "extensions":{}}
```

4. **Retry once** — base64-encode the compact JSON and send it in
   `PAYMENT-SIGNATURE`. Success is HTTP 200 with the bundle and a
   `PAYMENT-RESPONSE` settlement receipt.

If the paid request times out, preserve the error and any receipt.
Confirm payment status before creating or replaying an authorization.

### Legacy compatibility

Existing Solana and `X-PAYMENT` clients remain accepted. A legacy
Solana proof still has this shape:

```json
{"x402Version":2,"scheme":"exact","network":"solana","payload":{"signature":"5KtP...your tx signature...","payer":"9xQe...your wallet..."}}
```

public ledger and stats. Requires admin token. Irreversible.

paying customer. Purging it is refused unless the request explicitly sets

Delete all quality='canary' rows from eq_training_corpus and eq_wishlist.

Canary rows are written during automated self-test runs (see CANARY_PREFIXES /
CANARY_WISHLIST_PREFIX). The server back-fills them at startup, but rows that
arrive during a running deployment are not cleaned up until the next restart.
This endpoint lets an operator flush them on demand without a restart.

post.description:
Verify a Solana transaction signature on-chain and enforce double-spend protection.

1. Checks the local database for a previously verified occurrence of this signature.
2. If not seen, queries the public Solana RPC to confirm the signature exists on-chain.
3. Records the signature in solana_verified_signatures (idempotency key) to prevent reuse.

Returns the on-chain status plus whether this is a new or duplicate verification.
